S17.title: Höfn, Day 9. Four Jackets on One Rack

paragraphs.S17.C000.P000: They reached Höfn late in the afternoon. After the glacier lagoon, conversation in the car came and went: each of them was trying to hold on to their own impression without getting in the others' way. Alice watched a fingerprint trail on the fogged window. Nick drew a duck in it and insisted it was a map of tomorrow's road.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P001: “The duck is facing east?” Alice asked.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P002: “It is looking at us with disapproval. That's a universal direction.”
paragraphs.S17.C000.P003: Eric did not turn from the wheel.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P004: “If it plans to lead, it can check the forecast first.”
paragraphs.S17.C000.P005: The guesthouse smelled of wet wool and something fried. The owner showed them the shared kitchen, the washing machine in an alcove, and a note asking guests to clear the drying rack for whoever came next. They hung all four jackets on one rail; the rack swayed unhappily. Damir moved it closer to the wall. Nick announced that this was the group's first joint architectural project.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P006: Alice found a small black stone in her pocket from yesterday's walk. She did not remember picking it up, and set it on the sill so she could return it to the ground later instead of carrying it across a border with her receipts. Her notebook lay beside it. After eight days on the road, it held more notes about who had asked “Are you comfortable?” than about the views they had travelled to see.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P007: “There's soup,” Eric announced, looking in the fridge. “And bread. The owner said it's her dinner for guests if we get there before nine.”
paragraphs.S17.C000.P008: “‘If we get there’ sounds like a professional challenge,” Nick said.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P010: “All the more reason. I need a challenge I can handle.”
paragraphs.S17.C000.P011: The soup was thick and full of seafood; everyone served themselves. Nick asked for seconds before finishing his first bowl. Damir moved her notebook away from the edge of the table when Alice reached for the bread. He did not look at the open pages, and that was exactly what she noticed.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P012: At the next table, two women discussed a trip they had had to shorten because of the weather. One laughed too loudly, then said, “At least we made it here.” Alice saved the last words in her phone, but not their faces or someone else's story. The trip was full of decisions that did not belong to her.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P013: When dinner ended, the car was still under the window, its sides dusty. Eric spread a dry map of the next section across the table. His finger paused over the Eastfjords.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P014: “We stay here tomorrow,” he said. “Laundry, supplies, rest. We leave in the morning the day after. I need to check the road and the stop times once more.”
paragraphs.S17.C000.P015: “Thank you for a day without a suitcase,” Alice said.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P016: “You can carry the suitcase. I don't take responsibility for personal hobbies.”
paragraphs.S17.C000.P017: The kitchen laughed. Eric placed the map beside her notebook without covering it. In these past days she had learned to tell his caution from his wish to anticipate everything. The first warmed her; the second sometimes made her defend even her right to get wet.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P018: It turned out that only half a shelf was free on the drying rack. All four brought wet things from their rooms. Nick spread his heavy sweater across two sections: the sleeves would not fit any other way. Alice held a wet scarf and asked him to leave room for everyone else. Nick took the sweater down without arguing, but she was annoyed that she had needed to ask for something obvious. Damir brought two clean clothespins from his travel kit. Eric lifted the rack and showed them how to pull out a hidden section. Nick hung the sweater there, and Alice labelled strips of paper with the room numbers—no one would sort through someone else's shirts tomorrow.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P019: “It took us nine days to learn how to fold laundry as a team,” Nick observed.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P020: “We still haven't learned how to fold it,” Damir replied.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P021: The owner came in for her mug and nodded approvingly at the rack. Alice suddenly realised she had been smiling for several minutes. Nothing important had happened: they had eaten, wiped the table, cleared the passage. But if Marina asked when the trip had stopped being a collection of interviews, Alice might remember these wet sleeves.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P022: She remembered the promise made at the lagoon and opened her draft. Not the whole file: only three short passages where her companions might recognise themselves. Nick stopped turning a clothespin, Eric folded the map, and Damir dried his hands. Alice read Eric a line aloud: “At the signpost, he waited until everyone caught up, and only then named the time we would return.” Eric asked her to replace “named” with “suggested”: they had changed the time together later. She corrected it in front of him.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P023: She showed Damir the line: “The tourist's leg hurt; Damir helped her, and we were delayed.” He covered the second half with his finger.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P024: “You don't have permission to write about her. And don't write it as if I alone decided what she should do.”
paragraphs.S17.C000.P025: Alice deleted the line altogether. In its place was one verifiable shared detail: “We moved our departure back ten minutes and waited for one another by the car.” Damir nodded. She did not even open the private conversation after the rescue.
paragraphs.S17.C000.P026: She turned the screen toward Nick with the paragraph about how he had stopped the camera by the water.

S17.C001.title: S17-N-A — after S15-C1 A: the conversation stayed personal

paragraphs.S17.C001.P000: There was a blank space between two sentences. Nick ran a finger over it without touching the screen.
paragraphs.S17.C001.P002: “My guess about you was there. I crossed it out.”
paragraphs.S17.C001.P003: “Let it stay that way. The part about the camera is right, but show me the final version before you send it.”
paragraphs.S17.C001.P004: Alice put a note beside it—“show Nick”—without filling the space with someone else's confession.

S17.C002.title: S17-N-B — after S15-C1 B: only the observed action was approved

paragraphs.S17.C002.P000: Alice highlighted one sentence: “Nick asked before filming and lowered the camera when I entered the edge of the frame.” Nick read it twice.
paragraphs.S17.C002.P001: “That's more precise. I was filming the wide shot, you stepped in, and I lowered the camera. Don't add a scene that didn't happen.”
paragraphs.S17.C002.P002: Alice rewrote the verbs in front of him. Nick allowed her to keep the line, but asked her not to add the story about the former heroine. She closed the neighbouring note where she kept his confession.

S17.C003.title: S17-N-C — after S15-C1 C: the shared file waits for two permissions

paragraphs.S17.C003.P000: Nick showed her a file on his phone called “shore_without_voices”: a few seconds of ice and water at the lagoon, with no recognisable voices. In her draft, next to it, was “check before sending,” with no link to the file.
paragraphs.S17.C003.P001: “This piece works for me,” he said. “But my ‘yes’ is only for watching it now. Sending it is a separate question.”
paragraphs.S17.C003.P002: “And my ‘yes’ hasn't been given either. I won't attach the file to my email to Marina today.”
paragraphs.S17.C003.P003: He put the phone away. Alice showed him a separate sentence about his action; he corrected the verb tense, and she kept the change. The editor received no footage or sound yet.

paragraphs.S17.C004.P000: Alice closed the screen. Eric returned to the map, Nick put a clothespin on the rack, and Damir brought an empty mug from the hall.

S17.C005.title: S17-E-A — after S13-C1 A: Alice remains responsible for the draft

paragraphs.S17.C005.P000: “I'll send these lines to you again before the email to Marina,” Alice said. “I'm not asking you to approve the whole article. The recognisable part—yes, we'll check that.”
paragraphs.S17.C005.P001: Eric wrote her deadline in the margin of the map. Nick asked her not to send it at night. Alice marked that in her calendar: the responsibility for sending it remained hers.

S17.C006.title: S17-E-B — after S13-C1 B: collecting observations together

paragraphs.S17.C006.P000: “What from today would you give to the piece yourselves?” Alice asked.
paragraphs.S17.C006.P001: Eric named the rearranged drying rack, Nick named the argument about socks, and Damir named the ten minutes by the car. Alice wrote all three suggestions side by side, without presenting them as permission to use a biography or a close-up. Nick asked to keep the right to cross out his line later.

S17.C007.title: S17-D-A — after S16-C1 A: tea without a demand for a story

paragraphs.S17.C007.P000: Damir looked at the identical white guesthouse mugs.
paragraphs.S17.C007.P001: “There isn't the one with the whale. I should have asked them to sell yesterday's.”
paragraphs.S17.C007.P002: “It wouldn't have survived our car. And you don't need a good mug to have professional meaning.”
paragraphs.S17.C007.P003: He smirked and drank from the white mug. No one asked about the ten minutes after he helped the tourist.

S17.C008.title: S17-D-B — after S16-C1 B: the promised time was kept

paragraphs.S17.C008.P000: Damir returned to the table after a short call while the others were still sorting the laundry.
paragraphs.S17.C008.P001: “They did leave me a portion after all yesterday. Thank you.”
paragraphs.S17.C008.P002: “That's what we agreed,” Alice said. “Today's soup stays here until Nick carries off the seconds.”
paragraphs.S17.C008.P003: Damir sat down to finish eating while they completed their tasks. Alice did not ask what the call had been about: he still had a life beyond the shared kitchen.

S17.C009.title: Choice S17-C1 — Which part of the shared task will Alice take on

paragraphs.S17.C009.P000: One fragment is selected. This changes the group's brief response, but does not decide the evening or close any route.

paragraphs.S17.C010.P000: “Give me a pencil,” Alice said. “I'll mark where we really need to stop and where we've simply got used to stopping.”
paragraphs.S17.C010.P003: “For the necessary ones that look unnecessary.”
paragraphs.S17.C010.P004: She put a small circle by the waterfront. He did not erase it, and set the pencil down for her.

S17.C011.title: B. Sort the laundry with Nick

paragraphs.S17.C011.P000: “I'll handle the labelling system,” Alice said. “You can give it a ridiculous name.”
paragraphs.S17.C011.P001: Nick looked at the strips of paper.
paragraphs.S17.C011.P004: “Then just don't lose my only dry sweater.”
paragraphs.S17.C011.P005: He handed her the sweater and, for the first time that evening, did not reach for the camera when their hands met.

S17.C012.title: C. Make a kitchen arrangement with Damir

paragraphs.S17.C012.P000: “You wash and I'll dry?” Alice suggested.
paragraphs.S17.C012.P001: Damir looked over the pile of dishes.
paragraphs.S17.C012.P003: “Let's leave that part as it is.”
paragraphs.S17.C012.P004: They stood side by side. When his phone rang, Damir asked whether she was comfortable finishing alone. Before, he would already have left to answer it; now he waited for her “yes.”

S17.C013.title: D. Give everyone a task and keep a pause for herself

paragraphs.S17.C013.P000: “Choose one task each,” Alice said. “I'll finish my tea and come back to the table.”
paragraphs.S17.C013.P001: Nick took the dishes, Damir took the drying rack, and Eric took the map. Nick performed the distribution of powers like a ceremony. Alice stayed by the window for five minutes. No one asked her to justify those five minutes with usefulness.

paragraphs.S17.C014.P000: By evening, the window reflected the kitchen instead of the harbour. Eric asked whether Alice wanted to walk to the fire by the harbour entrance: it was close, if the weather allowed. Nick said the local pool was open late and showed her the hours on his phone; he would leave the camera in the room if she wanted. Damir suggested cooking dinner together tomorrow from ingredients they had not bought yet. Each invitation arrived in turn, without an audience or a vote.
paragraphs.S17.C014.P001: Alice could spend the time alone. For several days she had been carrying a letter to Marina in her drafts: not a report on kilometres, but a request to change the angle of the piece. She was not obliged to send it today. And yet her own plan was no less real than the three invitations.
paragraphs.S17.C014.P002: “I'll tell you in a minute,” she asked.
paragraphs.S17.C014.P003: She went into the hall, where the four jackets hung, and chose how to spend the free time before tomorrow's departure from Höfn: tonight with Eric or Nick, tomorrow evening with Damir, or both days on her own terms.
